answers.reset_and_flush: The process at 154 is sensitive to posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni. When rst_ni is low, status_cnt_q is asynchronously set to zero at 155-158. Otherwise a high flush_i sets status_cnt_q to zero on the rising clock edge at 161-165; reset has priority over flush. With neither asserted, the rising edge loads status_cnt_n at 168-171.

count_behavior.premises: For known counts in the normal occupancy range 0 through 8, full_o is (q==8) and empty_o is (q==0) at 68-70; FALL_THROUGH=0. The following describes the next q on a rising edge when reset is deasserted and flush is low. The combinational sequence and guards are at 75-79, 98-99, 116, 119, 127, and 130-131.
count_behavior.push_only: If q<8 the guarded push sets n=q+1; at q=8 the push is blocked and n=q.
count_behavior.pop_only: If q>0 the guarded pop sets n=q-1; at q=0 the pop is blocked and n=q.
count_behavior.simultaneous_push_and_pop: For 0<q<8 both operations are accepted and the final override sets n=q. At q=0, pop is blocked and push is accepted, so n=1. At q=8, push is blocked and pop is accepted, so n=7. Simultaneous requests at either boundary violate the source assertions forbidding push while full or pop while empty (222-228), which may terminate simulation.
count_behavior.neither: The initial n=q assignment remains in effect, so the count holds.

answers.read_modify_write: There is no source-level in-place read-modify-write assignment to status_cnt_q. The combinational process reads q and writes the distinct n signal at 116 and 127; the sequential process later reads n and writes q at 171. The semantic access index reports those q accesses separately as reads and writes, with no read_write access. The overall registered state does have arithmetic feedback across the two processes and clock edge, so it can be understood as a staged state update, but it is not an in-place q assignment or an increment/decrement operator applied to q.
